challenge.better_approach: A merge verb moving notes was looked at; the measured need is only that a duplicate stops holding BUILDME, and notes already cross-reference. withdraw is the smaller move.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That resolved=True with answer None is read as 'not a decision' everywhere. Measured: corrosion's citation.py refuses a resolved record without an answer; rung 4 in reseal.py does not, which is the sibling guard ticket.
challenge.prior_art: e1d3fd0f2aab (outlinecheck reuses an open question on the same Q#n) stops one source of duplicates; note and rebind in cairn/tools/question/question.py are the door's existing verbs.
challenge.real_collision: none: the write rides the question door (_write, verb answer), as answer and note do.

answers.falsifier: Done when a withdrawn duplicate leaves open_for(ticket) unanswered and every bad withdrawal is refused unchanged; wrong intent if a withdrawal can be cited as a decision.
answers.from_idea: none, because the live trouble question-has-no-withdraw-verb-for-a-duplicate (bin/cmd/trouble live) names the missing verb of bin/cmd/question as its residue
answers.how: withdraw(qid, duplicate_of, why) in cairn/tools/question/question.py and a withdraw subparser in its __main__.py; red-first proof cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_a_duplicate_question_is_withdrawn_unanswered.py.
answers.traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth stays true; an open duplicate says a decision is owed twice, and answering it to close it writes a decision nobody made.
answers.what: cairn question can withdraw an open question that duplicates another on the same ticket, resolving it with no answer and naming the question that stands.

bullets.text: Of the readers of a question's resolved field, only corrosion checks that an answer exists; rung 4 trusts resolved alone.
